workstream: U25 -- small, smooth actuator-response probes (NOT a training run)
motivation: Before justifying more training budget: does Cara respond predictably to reasonable commands? U24 improved survival/smoothness but left the actuator-path question open.
method: Same CaraWalkEnv model, resets (confirmed deterministic), and control timing (50Hz) as every other U19+ script. Four tests: (1) zero-action hold -- per-joint baseline; (2) fast smooth single-joint excursion (100ms ramp, 200ms hold, cubic smoothstep, zero endpoint velocity) and return; (3) same shape with a 400ms ramp; (4) replay of the actual U24 trained policy (deterministic mean), same per-joint instrumentation. Tested l_ankle_pitch, l_knee_pitch, l_hip_pitch individually (all other 11 actuators held at nominal). Excursion amplitude 0.4 (normalized action units) chosen to bracket U24's own mean |action|=0.3811.

1_zero_hold.note: No joint saturates at zero action. Clean baseline.

key_finding: Smooth commands (fast OR slow ramps) tracked well on every joint -- 0% saturation in all 6 excursion tests, tracking error 0.014-0.024 rad (~1-1.4 deg). The ankle and knee single-joint excursions DID cause falls (isolated, uncompensated single-joint perturbations with no balance strategy -- expected for this test design, not evidence of an actuator defect: tracking stayed accurate right up to and through the fall). U24's actual replayed commands are categorically different: peak per-joint velocity 2.5-5x HIGHER than even the fast smooth test (ankle: 6.22 vs 1.21 rad/s), tracking error 2-2.5x worse, and REAL saturation appears for the first time (ankle 20.6% of steps, 140ms longest continuous run) -- something none of the smooth tests produced on any joint.
decision: Commands track well under smooth, moderate-speed motion; poor tracking and saturation only appear when replaying the actual learned policy, whose commands (2.5-5x higher peak angular velocity, high-frequency step-to-step jitter even in the DETERMINISTIC mean output) are well outside the tested range. Per the given decision rule, this points to 'commands track well but the posture destabilizes Cara: return to policy coordination and reward incentives' -- specifically, nothing in the current reward (w_action_rate=0.01) or architecture is discouraging the high-frequency, high-velocity action pattern the policy has learned, and this appears to be what actually drives saturation/poor tracking, not an actuator/controller-path defect.
not_done_this_turn: No fix implemented, no new training run. This was diagnosis only, per the same pattern as U23 -- flagged for the next decision.
